title: dockato: water docked into the 200 DMSO + 400 water box
purpose: `dockato` [@epsrmanual] builds larger molecules from `.ato` building blocks: copies of the first molecule of a docking file are bonded onto free sites of a docked file, removing one atom of each to form the new bond. This case docks into a full simulation box, where the overlap test uses minimum-image distances.
fortran: `dockato.f`: `dockato` (driver, parameters from command line or stdin), `rotatem`, `random_rotatem`, `search_unsaturated`, `find_valence`
system: The EPSR-test configuration `200DMSO400Water.ato`: 200 DMSO (atoms S, C, C, O, 6 H) and 400 water molecules (O1, H1, H1; SPC/E parameters [@berendsen1987]), 3200 atoms at 300 K in a cubic box of side 33.12 Å, a model of the DMSO-water mixtures of Soper and Luzar [@soperluzar1992]. Atom `atomd` of the new molecule is placed on `atomv`, the molecule is rotated so that its `atomdr` neighbour lies on the `atomvr` neighbour of `atomv` (equal bond lengths required), an optional second (dihedral) rotation about the new bond uses `atomdrr`/`atomvrr` (random angle in [dminrr, dmaxrr] from `ran1`, the Park-Miller generator with Bays-Durham shuffle [@parkmiller1988,@numrec1992], or a fixed dihedral that creates a DIH group when dminrr = dmaxrr), overlaps are tested with a distance factor, `atomd` and `atomvr` are removed and the new rotational group, bonds and atom types are updated. A single water is bonded O-O onto one water of the box.
inputs: `WaterMolecule.ato` and `200DMSO400Water.ato` from EPSR-test, all parameters on the command line, one molecule per run (ndock = 1): run 1 dihedral 30-150°, factor 1.0; run 2 factor 0.6; run 3 overlaps allowed, fixed dihedral 60° (DIH group).
verification: Each run writes one new `.ato` file (coordinates, bonds, rotational groups, atom types and the random-number state), compared byte for byte with the stored Fortran output. With factor 1.0, hundreds of candidate water sites are rejected by `test_overlap` before one is accepted (README). Each output keeps 600 molecules and holds 3201 atoms (one water added, two H removed) and 401 rotational groups.
notes: Fortran behaviour reproduced: `nal(imv)` of the docked molecule is extended although the new atoms are at the end of the atom list, so molecule atom ranges overlap. With ndock > 1 on this box the Fortran writes `moltemplate(0)` (out of bounds); the port refuses that case, hence ndock = 1.
